# The Evolution of the Discourse: From Agentic Coding to Loop Engineering {#sec-discourse}

::: {.callout-warning}
## Drafting Status
Pre-draft · Owner: TBD. The brief below is the direction set by the teaching team; the owner will research and rewrite it.
:::

## What This Chapter Covers

As soon as the term "vibe coding" took hold, a flood of concepts emerged to refine or move past it: agentic coding, context engineering, spec-driven development, and, settling into place by mid-2026, loop engineering. Where prompt engineering asked "what do we say to the model," loop engineering asks "how do we design the system that lets an agent find its own work, do it, verify it, and remember it." This chapter traces the genealogy of these concepts and analyzes what bottleneck shift each one reflects.

## Seed Questions

- Who first formalized each concept (agentic coding, context engineering, spec-driven development, loop engineering), and when?
- What bottleneck moved each time the concept changed? (model capability → context → verification → loop design)
- Did these discourses actually change development practice, or just rename it?
- What is likely to be the next bottleneck?
